channel.title: Fuyao · Blog
channel.description: Business operations, cross-border growth and AI skill packs — field notes from running a 49-store, 9-brand operation.

item.title: An AI Skill Pack Is Not Finished When It Runs: Golden-Set Wilson Bounds and Weekly Control Limits as the Regression Gate
item.description: A regression post-mortem on a margin-diagnosis skill pack: 60 golden cases in four groups of 15, 43/60 (71.67%) on the first build, 57/60 (95.00%) after three repair rounds. A 95.00% point estimate only supports an 86.30% Wilson 95% lower bound, and clearing 95% needs 73 cases even with a perfect run. Over twelve weekly reruns W9 (51 cases) and W11 (50) break the 3-sigma limit, while a flat 95% line false-alarms twice in the eight-week baseline. 1,470 yuan of repair buys 14,784 yuan of monthly avoided loss, paid back in 2.98 days. Zero-dependency script included.

item.title: A Rebate You Have Not Collected Is Not Margin: Ladder Rebates, Realization Rate and the Restated Gross Margin
item.description: Six SKUs on 12.37M yuan of monthly revenue: top-tier accrual books 5.421M of gross profit at 43.82% while cash received is 5.143M at 41.58% - 278K yuan and 2.25 points of fiction, 3.336M annualised. Of 672.9K accrued rebate only 395.0K arrives, a 58.69% realization rate; 15% ad budget built on accrued margin overruns by 42K a month. Weighting tiers by twelve-month hit frequency cuts the error to 38K yuan (86.2% reduction), and 18% Q4 volume growth lifts realization to 79.76%. Includes a zero-dependency Python script.

item.title: Stop Sizing Safety Stock in Days: Service Level, Lead-Time Variance and the Stockout Cost Triangle
item.description: Safety stock set at 21 days implies z values from 1.45 to 5.04 and real service levels from 92.7% to 100% across six SKUs, at 74,857 yuan a year. Lead-time variance is 94.1% of demand-over-lead-time variance; ignore it and a 95% service level is understated by 76.9% (3,254 units computed as 753). Pricing holding against stockout cost puts optimal z at 2.47 to 2.59, cutting annual cost to 48,223 yuan (-35.58%) while capital rises from 172,221 to 194,338; with capital frozen, a uniform z of 2.22 still saves 23,861. Fixing three SKUs moves net capital 27 yuan and cuts cost 18,668. Includes a zero-dependency script.

item.title: Shipping Never Bills the Weight You Measure: A Dimensional-Weight Audit and the Repack Payback
item.description: A cushion that weighs 0.90kg bills at 12.50kg and costs 92.75 yuan a parcel, 31.0% of its 299-yuan price tag. With six SKUs, 8,740 orders and 1.76M yuan of monthly GMV, this piece separates volumetric weight, 0.5kg rounding, first-weight tiers and carrier divisors: a weight-only budget understates freight by 117,130 yuan (54.39%), while shrinking cartons and splitting carriers takes monthly freight from 332,495 to 236,060 yuan, a 96,435-yuan saving equal to 91.2% of net profit. Includes a zero-dependency Python script.

item.title: A Discount Is Not a Discount: Equivalent Rate and the Margin Floor Behind Promo Spend
item.description: Promo spend cannot be budgeted off the nominal rate. Across six stores and 24 order tiers, a 25% threshold promo is worth only 18.87% while a flat 12% cut costs 12.00%; the portfolio effective rate is 9.29% on 1.858M yuan of discounts. Solving the discount ceiling from the cost structure flags store S5 at 18.87% against a 16.00% ceiling with CM1 at 9.34%; stacking in low-margin stores takes CM1 from 21.12 to 3.45 yuan, and a flat 12% cut adds 173,000 yuan a month. Includes a zero-dependency Python script.

item.title: Cash Conversion Cycle: How DSO, DIO and DPO Turn Operating Reality into a Number
item.description: The cash conversion cycle is a liquidity check for operators, not a report metric. Six stores combined: monthly revenue 8.60M, cost of goods sold 6.02M, DSO 10.9 days, DIO 26.3 days, DPO 9.8 days, CCC 27.4 days, tied-up working capital 7.86M. Layered by store, store F holds 14.1% of the cash on 4.0% of revenue at 97.8 days of CCC. Capping DIO at 30 days releases 674,000 yuan, with four data traps and a zero-dependency script.

item.title: SKU Turnover Layering: Layer First, Cut Later When Pruning the Long Tail
item.description: Inventory is cash already spent. Layer SKU turnover and cut SKUs on separate conventions: 30 live SKUs sliced by cumulative revenue at 70/90/99, layer A holds 5 SKUs with 71.2% of revenue at 0.74 monthly turns, while 20 SKUs in layers C+D tie up 23.0% of inventory value on 9.1% of revenue. A dual gate of 0.3 turns and 3,000 yuan isolates 17 hits, 10 exemptions and 7 real cuts, releasing 54,515 yuan (9.4% of total), with three exemption rules and a zero-dependency Python layering script.

item.title: Return Rate Is Not an After-Sales Metric: Counting Reverse Logistics into Net Goods Value
item.description: Return rate is a deduction from net goods value, not an after-sales metric. Five cost blocks — refund, reverse logistics, packaging loss, customer-service labor, resale markdown — applied to four home-storage SKUs: the top-selling wall rack has 18.5% returns and only 75.0% net goods value, 16.1 points below the folding box. Includes zero-dependency Python, reason tags and thresholds.

item.title: Ad Creative A/B Testing: Bayesian Decisions on Material Survival
item.description: Ad creative testing should not be a gut call. AI-generated material variants, micro-budget 72-hour rapid tests, CTR decay rate and Bayesian A/B decisions: in 7 days one home-goods line tested 8 material sets; a high-contrast color block won with 3.2% CTR, 4.5 ROAS and 100% posterior win probability, while losers went into a negative-constraint library. Includes zero-dependency reproducible Python code.

item.title: Dynamic Ad Budget Reallocation: Move Money by Marginal ROI
item.description: An ad budget is not a one-time split. Reallocate by marginal ROI: a dynamic budget pool with 40/50/10 weights, 5 misallocation signals, and a reproducible Python simulator — same 50K daily budget, 5 iterations lift weighted mROI from 2.47 to 2.77, adding 14,900 RMB of daily profit.

item.title: Cash Flow Baseline Management: Stress-Test the Multi-Store Matrix Before Scaling
item.description: Profit on paper is not cash in hand. Define the cash flow baseline as monthly rigid costs times safety months, compare sea vs air capital occupation, and stress-test 12 weeks with pandas — delayed logistics and lagged payments turn 7 of 12 weeks red before cash runs out. Full reproducible code included.

item.title: ACOS Tiered Management for Amazon Ads: Turning Daily Bid Adjustments into an AI Skill
item.description: ACOS is not always lower-is-better. Sort SKUs into traffic, profit, clearance and defense tiers by gross margin, set a target ACOS per tier, scan the weekly ad report with reproducible Python, get over-threshold alerts and bid suggestions, then package the routine as an AI skill with a SKILL.md template.

item.title: Don't Just Review GMV: A Five-Layer Net Profit Breakdown as an AI Skill
item.description: GMV is an order metric, not cash. A five-layer net profit breakdown — refunds, take rate, logistics, ads, fixed cost — takes 860K GMV down to net profit with reproducible Python and a SKILL.md template.
